chunks: Praise be to Allah, the One in whom I have not become dead nor sick,
nor have my veins been struck with evil, nor have I been taken for the worst of my deeds,
nor is my progeny cut off, nor have I reverted from my religion,
nor do I deny my Lord, nor do I feel strangeness in my faith,
nor is my intellect confused, nor have I been punished with the punishment of the nations before me.
I have become a slave, owned (by You), wronging myself,
You have the argument against me and I have no argument (against You),
I cannot take except what You have given me,
and I cannot ward off except what You have saved me from.

key_terms.مَضْرُوبًا عَلَى عُرُوقِي: struck on the veins (referring to disease or affliction)

ai.seo_question: What is the morning supplication of gratitude and humility in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This morning supplication (Du'a al-Sabah) from Nahj al-Balagha reflects the Shia tradition of starting the day with self-accountability (muhasaba), acknowledging that while one is a servant, they are also their own worst enemy due to negligence. It emphasizes the concept of 'Hujjah' (divine proof/argument) resting with God, reinforcing the balance between human free will and divine mercy, a key theme in Shia theology regarding the Day of Judgment.
